transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (HelixHealth ML Lead), Carlos Mendes (HelixHealth Platform), Janelle Ruiz (HelixHealth Product)

Summary: Quick POC weekly sync to review last week's benchmark results across model variants, discuss pinning strategy and rollback/fallback policies, and align on next steps for canary. Customer wants to pick a pinned model for the pilot and ensure an automated fallback path to a quantized or cheaper variant if latency/cost/regressions occur.

Topics: model selection, version pinning, rollback/fallback policies, latency vs cost tradeoffs, QA failures, staging benchmarks, observability for canary.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 40 minutes, quick agenda - results review, tuning notes, and next steps for pinning.
[00:12] Priya: yep, thanks. we ran the 1k prompts you gave last week, quick summary - the open model v1.2.0 has best quality but spikes in p95 latency on longer context, the quantized 1.2.0-q has similar medians but lower cost.
[00:30] Liam: got it. can you call out the p95 numbers?
[00:33] Priya: median is about 180ms per token, p95 was 1.2s for the full 2k context we tested, whereas the q variant hit p95 around 850ms. but there were a few hallucination cases in the q variant, about 2.1% of the prompts.
[00:49] Maya: okay that's helpful. Carlos, did you capture the infra variance - were requests hitting Dedicated pool or shared?
[00:54] Carlos: staging was on Dedicated-equivalent nodes, same GPU types, we used the Redwood dedicated pool config you suggested, but we had autoscale 0.
[01:05] Janelle: so the business question - do we pick the higher-quality open model and accept higher p95, or pin to q variant and mitigate hallucinations with rerank/filters?
[01:15] Priya: we prefer quality, but the production SLO for user flows is 800ms p95. the open model breaches that.
[01:23] Liam: couple options we recommended earlier - pin to v1.2.0 in staging but enable automatic fallback to 1.2.0-q for requests that exceed latency threshold, or route percent of traffic to q for cost experiments. We also have model variant rollbacks if regression detected by eval hooks.
[01:38] Maya: also worth noting you can pin by route, so search can use q variant while compose uses full model.
[01:44] Priya: how mature are the automatic eval hooks? we saw some false positives last week where minor token diffs flagged regression.
[01:51] Liam: fair. the current eval hooks can be tuned - threshold, metric windows, and requiring multiple failing prompts to trigger rollback. we should set the detection sensitivity to avoid noisy rollbacks.
[02:04] Priya: would be great if we could see per-prompt regression examples inline in the alert.
[02:09] Liam: yes, we can include the top failing prompts and diffed outputs in the alert payload.
[02:14] Maya: for canary, recommended pattern: 5% traffic to pinned model in prod with detailed tracing for 72 hours, automatic rollback if error rate or metric regressions exceed thresholds, otherwise bump to 25 then 100.
[02:26] Carlos: question on fallback - if the pinned model is unavailable, can Redwood automatically fall back to the hosted variant in another region?
[02:33] Liam: yes, routing policy supports region fallback and capacity-tier fallback. you can define order: pinned -> quantized variant -> hosted-compatible open variant in another region. there's an associated cost delta though.
[02:47] Janelle: any limitations on KV cache coherence across fallback hops? last week we saw some weird prefixes missing when switching nodes.
[02:55] Liam: that was likely a cache TTL mismatch - when we route to a different instance without shared KV cache the prefix won't be present; we recommend prefix-level cache warming and conservative TTLs if you expect hot fallbacks.
[03:08] Priya: okay noted. another data point - our quality eval (ROUGE/QA pass) on v1.2.0 is 88% while q variant is 84%. the team wants to keep quality above 86 ideally.
[03:21] Maya: so leaning to pinned v1.2.0 in staging, with canary and fallback to 1.2.0-q, but set rollback tolerances to avoid flapping.
[03:31] Priya: can we get a simple config snippet for pin + fallback? that would help our infra team implement quickly.
[03:36] Liam: I'll drop a config example - basically a route config with model_version: 1.2.0, fallback: [1.2.0-q, 1.1.9-eco], latency_threshold_ms: 800, rollback_criteria: {error_rate: 1.5%, quality_drop: 3%}, and an eval window 60min. (laughter) — apologies, that's me paraphrasing, I'll send exact yaml.
[03:55] Maya: great. Priya, can you share the top failure cases so we can triage whether they're prompt engineering or model regressions?
[04:02] Priya: yes, we'll annotate the 20 highest-severity failures and mark which are likely prompt issues.
[04:08] Carlos: on the infra side, i need instructions on quantization settings (8-bit vs 4-bit) used in test so we can match in staging.
[04:14] Liam: in the tests we used 8-bit symmetric quantization with AVX kernels; we can try 4-bit for a follow-up if you want more cost savings but quality may drop.
[04:23] Janelle: does Redwood provide automatic recommendations for quantization profiles?
[04:27] Maya: yes, Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching parameters based on workload; we'll surface the recommended profile in the benchmark sheet.
[04:34] Priya: let's talk about observability — we need per-route token cost, per-request trace id, and the raw outputs stored for 30 days for QA. is that possible?
[04:44] Maya: yes, token-level cost + traces are in the Console; retention is configurable, and we can enable event streaming to your S3 for 30 days. there are compliance knobs for PII redaction if needed.
[04:55] Carlos: last thing - latency in eu-west region is ~20% higher for us. we might prefer a US region for better p95, but data residency requires EU for some customers. tradeoff.
[05:06] Priya: we can start with EU staging for compliance but canary some traffic via US region for beta users.
[05:12] Maya: ok, to recap next steps - we'll send benchmark sheet and config examples, HelixHealth runs the pinned model QA, and we'll meet for canary rollout planning next week.
[05:23] Janelle: thanks everyone.
